items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My two kids, Edwin, who’s a very great jazz bass player and composer, and George, who’s a drummer

ctx.x: I want to take a left turn. We’ve talked about all of the hats that you’ve worn throughout your life. I want to talk about the hat that you wear as a family man, as a husband, and as a father, because you have two sons who have followed in your footsteps, and I know your relationship with your wife was a longstanding one. If you want to get a little personal, but certainly how George and Ed have been carrying on, and your feelings about them.

As for my wife, we met in Cincinnati when I was in the orchestra and therefore teaching at the conservatory there. I taught horn. She was – we were both 17. She was a student and a double major, piano and voice. I was on the faculty. We got together, and we were together 50 years. We first lived in New York, until I came to the Conservatory. I always said to Margie, if we ever leave New York, there’s only two places we can possible go. One is Boston, because of its cultural life and its history, and as an…

He was, as I say, not involved with music. He didn’t like school, and he cut a lot of classes. I didn’t know that. I just found out later. I was very upset. One day, he was – there was a music class led by a cellist here in Boston, a teacher who taught almost all the subjects and had a little orchestra also. All those schools in those days had orchestras. Most of them have disappeared nowadays. Edwin was standing out in the corridor, listening to the music in the room. As I say, he didn’t know anything about…
